q: The Estimates Committee of Parliament examines the estimates of the Ministries in order to report, among other things:

options.A: Whether the Appropriation Accounts have been correctly prepared
options.B: Whether all the audit objections raised by the Comptroller and Auditor General have been settled
options.C: The rate of dividend payable by the Railways to the General Revenues
options.D: Whether the money is well laid out within the limits of the policy implied in the estimates, and what economies and improvements in organisation and efficiency can be effected

e: The Estimates Committee reports on whether the money is well laid out within the policy implied in the estimates and suggests economies and improvements in organisation, efficiency and administrative reform; examining audit objections or the dividend rate is not its function.

q: Re-appropriation of funds from one head to another within a grant is effected:

options.A: Only with the prior approval of Parliament
options.B: By the competent executive authority under the powers delegated for the purpose, without the approval of Parliament
options.C: Only with the approval of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Only through a Supplementary Demand for Grant

e: Re-appropriation is an executive act: the competent authority diverts funds from one head to another within the same grant under delegated powers, so neither Parliament's approval nor a Supplementary Demand is needed.

q: Apportionment of the earnings of through traffic among the zonal railways is carried out:

options.A: Once a year, at the time of closing of the annual accounts
options.B: Every month, through the Traffic Book compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office
options.C: Only at the time of preparation of the Budget Estimates
options.D: Half-yearly, through the Debt Head Report

e: Apportionment of through-traffic earnings among the zonal railways is carried out every month through the Traffic Book compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office, not at the year end or budget stage.

q: Apportionment of earnings among the zonal railways is carried out in respect of:

options.A: Coaching earnings and Goods earnings
options.C: All earnings, including Sundry Other Earnings

e: Only coaching earnings and goods earnings of through traffic are apportioned among the railways concerned; sundry earnings are excluded from apportionment altogether.

q: Before the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the grants voted for the Railways were authorised to be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India through:

options.A: The general Appropriation Act of the Union
options.B: An executive order of the Railway Minister

e: Before the merger, railway grants were withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India through a separate Appropriation (Railways) Act passed after the Railway Demands were voted.

q: The cash equivalent of leave salary (leave encashment) payable on retirement to a railway servant covered under the old pension scheme is debited to:

options.A: The State Railway Provident Fund

e: Leave encashment on retirement is a pensionary benefit for staff under the old pension scheme, so it is debited to the Railway Pension Fund.

q: Under the Separation Convention of 1924, in addition to a fixed dividend on the capital-at-charge, the Railways were required to contribute to the General Revenues:

options.A: One-half of their surplus profits
options.D: The whole of their surplus profits

e: Under the Separation Convention of 1924, besides the fixed dividend on capital-at-charge, the Railways contributed one-fifth of their surplus profits to the General Revenues.

q: The Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement, required to be laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act, is presented:

options.A: In the Session of Parliament following the Budget Session
options.B: Along with the Annual Financial Statement in the Budget Session itself

e: The Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement under the FRBM Act is laid before Parliament in the session following the Budget Session, not along with the Budget itself.

q: The Contingency Fund of India, established under Article 267 of the Constitution, is in the nature of:

options.A: A part of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: A loan raised from the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: A fund in the Public Account, the balance of which lapses at the end of every year
options.D: An imprest placed at the disposal of the President, to enable advances to be made for meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament

e: The Contingency Fund of India is an imprest at the disposal of the President for advances to meet unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament; the advances are later recouped to the Fund.

q: If the Rajya Sabha does not return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha within fourteen days of its receipt, the Bill is:

options.A: Referred to a Joint Committee of both Houses
options.B: Deemed to have been passed by both Houses of Parliament in the form in which it was passed by the Lok Sabha
options.D: Returned to the President for reconsideration

e: A Money Bill not returned by the Rajya Sabha within fourteen days is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Lok Sabha.

q: The adoption (carrying) of a cut motion on a Demand for Grant in the Lok Sabha amounts to:

options.A: A mere suggestion which the Government may ignore
options.B: An increase in the amount of the Demand
options.C: A vote of censure against the Government, expressing disapproval of the policy underlying the Demand
options.D: Automatic passing of the Appropriation Bill

e: Adoption of a cut motion is treated as a vote of censure on the Government, expressing the Lok Sabha's disapproval of the policy underlying the Demand for Grant.

q: The appropriations to be made to the Development Fund and the Capital Fund of the Railways out of the year's surplus are determined:

options.A: At the close of the financial year, with reference to the actual surplus (net revenue) available for the year
options.B: In the Budget Estimates, as a fixed percentage of the gross earnings
options.C: By the Railway Convention Committee, once in five years
options.D: Monthly, in equal instalments throughout the year

e: Appropriations to the Development Fund and the Capital Fund are made only at the close of the year, with reference to the actual surplus (net revenue) available for that year.

q: The 'principal book' of account of a railway, in which accounts are maintained for all the heads of account and from which the Trial Balance is extracted, is the:

options.A: Main Cash Book

e: The Ledger is the principal book in which accounts are maintained for all heads of account, and the Trial Balance is extracted from it to prove arithmetical accuracy.

q: Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways are not apportioned among the zonal railways because:

options.A: They are too small in amount to be apportioned
options.B: They accrue wholly to the railway on which they arise, being in the nature of local and miscellaneous receipts which do not arise from the carriage of traffic over more than one railway
options.C: They are accounted for centrally by the Railway Board
options.D: They form part of the Public Account of India

e: Sundry Other Earnings arise wholly on the railway where they accrue, being local and miscellaneous receipts not earned by carrying traffic over more than one railway, so there is nothing to apportion.

q: The presentation of the Union Budget was advanced to the 1st of February (with effect from the Budget for 2017-18) primarily in order to:

options.A: Synchronise the Budget with the calendar year
options.B: Enable the Finance Bill to be passed within seventy-five days of its introduction
options.C: Complete the entire budgetary process — voting of the Demands and passing of the Appropriation Act — before the commencement of the financial year on the 1st of April, so that funds are available to the Ministries from the very beginning of the year
options.D: Avoid the need for a Vote on Account in election years

e: Presenting the Budget on 1 February allows the voting of Demands and the passing of the Appropriation Act to be completed before 1 April, so funds are available to Ministries from the first day of the financial year.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'budgetary control' from 'exchequer control' over railway expenditure?

options.A: Budgetary control is control over expenditure with reference to the grants voted by Parliament and the allotments made thereunder, whereas exchequer control regulates the actual cash outgo with reference to the ways and means position of the Government
options.B: Budgetary control is exercised by the Reserve Bank of India, whereas exchequer control is exercised by the Railway Board
options.C: Budgetary control relates only to capital expenditure, whereas exchequer control relates only to revenue expenditure
options.D: Budgetary control is exercised after the close of the financial year, whereas exchequer control is exercised before the Budget is presented

e: Budgetary control checks expenditure against the grants voted and the allotments made under them, whereas exchequer control regulates the actual cash outgo in line with the Government's ways and means position.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'surrender' of funds from 're-appropriation' of funds?

options.A: Surrender means diverting savings from one head to another within the same grant, whereas re-appropriation means returning savings to the grant
options.B: Surrender means giving up savings out of a grant so that they are no longer available to the surrendering unit, whereas re-appropriation means diverting savings under one head of a grant to meet expenditure under another head of the same grant
options.C: Surrender can be made only by Parliament, whereas re-appropriation can be made only at the close of the financial year
options.D: There is no difference between the two; both terms mean the transfer of funds from one grant to another

e: Surrender means giving up savings so that they cease to be available to the surrendering unit, whereas re-appropriation diverts savings under one head of a grant to meet expenditure under another head of the same grant.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Financial Bill' from a 'Money Bill'?

options.A: A Financial Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament, whereas a Money Bill can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha
options.B: A Financial Bill deals only with the matters enumerated in Article 110, whereas a Money Bill deals with taxation as well as other matters
options.C: A Money Bill deals exclusively with the matters enumerated in Article 110, whereas a Financial Bill contains some of those matters along with other matters and, after introduction in the Lok Sabha, is passed broadly like an ordinary Bill
options.D: A Financial Bill requires the prior recommendation of the President, whereas a Money Bill does not

e: A Money Bill deals exclusively with the matters in Article 110, while a Financial Bill contains some of those matters along with other matters and, after introduction in the Lok Sabha, is passed broadly like an ordinary Bill.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'PAO Suspense' from 'AG Suspense' in railway accounts?

options.A: PAO Suspense relates to transactions with State Governments, whereas AG Suspense relates to transactions with other Ministries of the Government of India
options.B: PAO Suspense is a remittance head, whereas AG Suspense is a debt head
options.C: PAO Suspense is operated only in the books of the Railway Board, whereas AG Suspense is operated only by the zonal railways
options.D: PAO Suspense is operated for transactions with the Pay and Accounts Offices of other Ministries and Departments of the Government of India pending settlement, whereas AG Suspense is operated for adjustments with State Governments and Accountants General pending settlement

e: PAO Suspense is operated for transactions with the Pay and Accounts Offices of other Ministries and Departments pending settlement, while AG Suspense covers adjustments with State Governments and Accountants General pending settlement.

q: In the Works Programme (Pink Book), which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'outlay' on a work from its 'throw-forward'?

options.A: The outlay is the amount provided for expenditure on the work during the year, whereas the throw-forward is the balance of the sanctioned cost which will remain to be incurred in the subsequent years
options.B: The outlay is the total sanctioned cost of the work, whereas the throw-forward is the expenditure already incurred on it
options.C: The outlay relates to works already completed, whereas the throw-forward relates to works not yet sanctioned
options.D: The outlay is provided by the Railway Board, whereas the throw-forward is provided by the zonal railway

e: In the Pink Book, the outlay is the amount provided for expenditure on a work during the year, whereas the throw-forward is the balance of the sanctioned cost still to be incurred in subsequent years.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Committee on Public Undertakings consists of twenty-two members, fifteen drawn from the Lok Sabha and seven from the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Committee examines the reports and accounts of the public undertakings, including the railway public sector undertakings, and the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India thereon.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Both statements are correct: the Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members - 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha - and it examines the reports and accounts of public undertakings and the CAG's reports on them.

q: The Public Accounts Committee examines the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways primarily in order to satisfy itself that:

options.A: The estimates for the ensuing year have been framed on a realistic basis
options.B: The moneys disbursed were legally available for, and applicable to, the service or purpose to which they were applied
options.C: The works included in the Works Programme have been executed according to the sanctioned estimates
options.D: The earnings of the Railways have been apportioned correctly among the zonal railways

e: The Public Accounts Committee examines the Appropriation Accounts to satisfy itself that the moneys disbursed were legally available for, and applicable to, the service or purpose for which the grants were made.

q: Which of the following is NOT a document presented to Parliament along with the annual Budget?

options.A: The Annual Financial Statement

e: The Appropriation Accounts are prepared after the close of the year from the actual accounts; they are not one of the documents presented along with the Budget, unlike the Annual Financial Statement, Demands for Grants and the Finance Bill.

q: 'Railways' is a subject in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution under Entry:
e: 'Railways' appears as Entry 22 in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.

q: The Railway Board, which exercises the powers of the Central Government in respect of the Government Railways, was set up under:

options.A: The Indian Railways Act, 1890

e: The Railway Board was set up under the Indian Railway Board Act, 1905 to exercise the powers of the Central Government in respect of the Government Railways.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cash balances of the Railways form part of the overall cash balance of the Government of India with the Reserve Bank of India.
2. Each zonal railway maintains a separate ways and means account with the Reserve Bank of India, distinct from the cash balance of the Government of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Statement 1 is correct: the cash balances of the Railways form part of the overall cash balance of the Government of India with the Reserve Bank of India. Statement 2 is false: no zonal railway maintains a separate ways and means account.

q:
Consider the following statements about the apportionment of earnings in the Traffic Book:
1. Charges for terminal services, rendered at the originating or terminating station, are retained by the railway which renders the service and are not apportioned.
2. The remaining (line-haul) earnings of through traffic are apportioned among the railways concerned in proportion to the distance travelled over each railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Both statements are correct: charges for terminal services are retained by the railway rendering the service, and the remaining line-haul earnings of through traffic are apportioned in proportion to the distance travelled over each railway.

q: The original grant under a Demand is Rs 1,350 crore. During the year, a supplementary grant of Rs 95 crore is obtained and funds of Rs 60 crore are surrendered. The Final Grant for the Demand is:

options.A: Rs 1,315 crore

e: Working: Final Grant = Original Grant + Supplementary Grant - Surrender = 1,350 + 95 - 60 = Rs 1,385 crore.

q: The Final Grant under a Demand for a year is Rs 720 crore and the actual expenditure booked against the Demand is Rs 758 crore. The excess expenditure which will require regularisation through an Excess Grant is:

options.A: Rs 28 crore

e: Working: Excess expenditure = Actual expenditure - Final Grant = 758 - 720 = Rs 38 crore, which requires regularisation through an Excess Grant.

q: Through-traffic earnings of Rs 15,000 are to be apportioned among Railways X, Y and Z in proportion to the distances travelled over them, namely 800 km, 450 km and 250 km respectively. The share of Railway Z is:
e: Working: Total distance = 800 + 450 + 250 = 1,500 km. Share of Railway Z = 15,000 x 250/1,500 = Rs 2,500.

q: The annual allotment for a head of account is Rs 840 crore and the budget proportion fixed for the first quarter of the year is 25 per cent. The proportionate allotment for the first quarter is:

options.A: Rs 168 crore

e: Working: Proportionate allotment = 25 per cent of Rs 840 crore = Rs 210 crore.

q: The gross earnings of a zonal railway for a year are Rs 3,600 crore. Refunds of fares and freight granted during the year amount to Rs 45 crore and are treated as a reduction of earnings. The net earnings credited in the accounts are:

options.A: Rs 3,645 crore

e: Working: Net earnings = Gross earnings - Refunds = 3,600 - 45 = Rs 3,555 crore, since refunds of fares and freight are treated as a reduction of earnings.

q: The annual plan outlay of the Railways is Rs 2,75,000 crore. It is financed by Gross Budgetary Support of Rs 1,50,000 crore and Extra Budgetary Resources of Rs 75,000 crore. The balance met from the internal resources of the Railways is:

options.A: Rs 25,000 crore

e: Working: Internal resources = Plan outlay - Gross Budgetary Support - Extra Budgetary Resources = 2,75,000 - 1,50,000 - 75,000 = Rs 50,000 crore.

q: The Final Grant under a Demand is Rs 640 crore and the actual expenditure is Rs 608 crore. The saving, expressed as a percentage of the Final Grant, is:

options.A: 5 per cent

e: Working: Saving = 640 - 608 = Rs 32 crore. Saving as percentage of Final Grant = 32/640 x 100 = 5 per cent.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the stages of the Budget in Parliament?

options.A: General discussion, Voting of Demands, examination by the Standing Committees, Appropriation Bill, Finance Bill
options.B: Presentation of the Budget, general discussion, examination by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees, Voting of Demands, Appropriation Bill, Finance Bill
options.C: Presentation of the Budget, Voting of Demands, general discussion, Finance Bill, Appropriation Bill
options.D: Voting of Demands, Presentation of the Budget, Appropriation Bill, general discussion, Finance Bill

e: The correct sequence is: presentation of the Budget, general discussion, examination of the Demands by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees, voting of the Demands, the Appropriation Bill and then the Finance Bill.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. When a station remits its earnings to the bank or the Cash Office, the amount is debited to 'Cash-in-Transit' in the railway books.
2. The 'Cash-in-Transit' is cleared when the amount is credited by the bank and taken to account under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank'.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Both statements are correct: earnings remitted by a station are debited to 'Cash-in-Transit', and the head is cleared when the bank credits the amount and it is taken to account under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank'.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Indian Railway Finance Code from the Indian Railway Accounts Code?

options.A: The Finance Code deals with Traffic Accounts, whereas the Accounts Code deals with the classification of accounts
options.B: The Finance Code is issued by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas the Accounts Code is issued by the Ministry of Finance
options.C: The Finance Code prescribes the forms of account books, whereas the Accounts Code prescribes the financial rules for the sanction of expenditure
options.D: The Finance Code lays down the financial rules, including the classification of accounts, whereas the Accounts Code prescribes the forms of accounts, the books to be maintained and the procedure for the compilation and rendering of accounts

e: The Finance Code lays down the financial rules, including the classification of accounts, whereas the Accounts Code prescribes the forms of accounts, the books to be maintained and the procedure for compilation and rendering of accounts.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Grant' from an 'Allotment' in railway budgeting?

options.A: A grant is the amount voted by Parliament for a Demand for Grant, whereas an allotment is the distribution of that grant by the Railway Board among the zonal railways and other units for incurring expenditure
options.B: A grant is made by the Railway Board to the zonal railways, whereas an allotment is made by Parliament to the Ministry of Railways
options.C: A grant relates to revenue expenditure only, whereas an allotment relates to capital expenditure only
options.D: A grant is valid for three years, whereas an allotment is valid for one year only

e: A grant is the amount voted by Parliament against a Demand for Grant, whereas an allotment is the distribution of that grant by the Railway Board among the zonal railways and other units for incurring expenditure.

q: The balance under the head 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' in the books of a zonal railway is invariably:

options.A: A credit balance, representing amounts payable to the Reserve Bank
options.B: A debit balance, representing the cash balance of the railway held with the Bank
options.C: Nil at the end of every month
options.D: A debit balance in the first half of the year and a credit balance in the second half

e: 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' invariably shows a debit balance because it represents the railway's cash balance held with the Bank, i.e. an amount standing to the railway's credit with the Bank.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Finance Bill from the Appropriation Bill?

options.A: The Finance Bill authorises withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas the Appropriation Bill gives effect to the taxation proposals of the Budget
options.B: The Finance Bill is introduced after the Appropriation Act has been passed, whereas the Appropriation Bill is introduced along with the Budget
options.C: The Finance Bill gives effect to the financial (taxation) proposals of the Budget, whereas the Appropriation Bill authorises the withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet the grants voted and the expenditure charged thereon
options.D: The Finance Bill is presented only in an election year, whereas the Appropriation Bill is presented every year

e: The Finance Bill gives effect to the financial (taxation) proposals of the Budget, whereas the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India for the grants voted and the expenditure charged on it.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A grant voted by Parliament lapses at the close of the financial year, and its unspent balance cannot be carried forward to the next year.
2. The balances accumulated in the Railway Funds, such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Development Fund, do not lapse at the close of the year and are carried forward.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Both statements are correct: a grant voted by Parliament lapses at the close of the financial year, but the balances in Railway Funds such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund and Development Fund do not lapse and are carried forward.

q: For meeting urgent and unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament, the Railways obtain advances from:

options.A: The Contingency Fund of India, there being no separate Contingency Fund for the Railways
options.B: A separate Railway Contingency Fund maintained by the Railway Board

e: There is no separate Contingency Fund for the Railways, so urgent and unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament is met by advances from the Contingency Fund of India.

q: After a bill has been paid, the voucher in support of the payment is stamped 'Paid' and cancelled primarily in order to:

options.A: Enable the voucher to be destroyed immediately after payment
options.B: Help the Cash & Pay Office in preparing the Cash Book
options.C: Indicate that the voucher has been checked by Audit
options.D: Prevent the same voucher from being presented again in support of another claim for payment

e: Stamping a paid voucher 'Paid' and cancelling it prevents the same voucher from being presented again in support of another claim for payment.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Finance Accounts of the Railways from their Balance Sheet?

options.A: The Finance Accounts are prepared by the zonal railways, whereas the Balance Sheet is prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: The Finance Accounts present the receipts and disbursements of the year under the Major Heads of account in the Government form, whereas the Balance Sheet is a statement of the assets and liabilities of the Railways, including the Block Account and the balances of the Railway Funds
options.C: The Finance Accounts relate to capital transactions only, whereas the Balance Sheet relates to revenue transactions only
options.D: The Finance Accounts are presented to Parliament, whereas the Balance Sheet is never disclosed outside the Railway Board

e: The Finance Accounts present the year's receipts and disbursements under the Major Heads of account, whereas the Balance Sheet is a statement of the assets and liabilities of the Railways, including the Block Account and the balances of the Railway Funds.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. After the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the budget proposals of the Railways are presented to Parliament by the Finance Minister as part of the Union Budget.
2. Before the merger, the separate Railway Budget used to be presented to Parliament by the Railway Minister.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Both statements are correct: after the merger the Finance Minister presents the railway proposals as part of the Union Budget, whereas before the merger the Railway Minister presented a separate Railway Budget.

q: Since the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the grants voted for the Railways are authorised to be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India through:

options.A: The common Appropriation Act of the Government of India, there being no separate Appropriation (Railways) Act
options.B: A separate Appropriation (Railways) Act passed every year
options.C: An order issued by the Railway Board
options.D: The Finance Act alone, without any Appropriation Act

e: Since the merger, railway grants are authorised to be withdrawn through the common Appropriation Act of the Government of India; a separate Appropriation (Railways) Act is no longer passed.

q: The sanctioned cost of a work is Rs 500 crore. Expenditure of Rs 320 crore has been incurred on it up to the end of the previous year and an outlay of Rs 80 crore is provided in the current year. The throw-forward of the work at the end of the current year will be:

options.A: Rs 180 crore

e: Working: Throw-forward = Sanctioned cost - Expenditure already incurred - Current year's outlay = 500 - 320 - 80 = Rs 100 crore.

q: The apportionment of through-traffic earnings among the zonal railways is effected:

options.A: By actual transfer of cash from the railway which collected the earnings to the other railways concerned
options.B: By adjustment through the Reserve Bank of India, which debits and credits the separate accounts of the railways
options.C: Only once a year, through the Balance Sheet of the Railways
options.D: Entirely by book adjustment through transfer transactions, without any physical transfer of cash between the railways

e: Apportionment of earnings is effected entirely by book adjustment through transfer transactions between the railways concerned; no cash is physically transferred.

q: In the erstwhile separate Railway Budget, Demand No. 15 related to:

options.A: Appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: In the erstwhile separate Railway Budget, Demand No. 15 related to Open Line Works - Revenue.

q: If the amount of a grant sanctioned by Parliament is required to be increased during the year, the increase can be effected only by:

options.A: An order of the Railway Board issued with the concurrence of the Financial Commissioner
options.B: A Supplementary Grant voted by Parliament
options.C: Re-appropriation of savings available under another grant
options.D: An order of the Ministry of Finance issued under the General Financial Rules

e: A grant sanctioned by Parliament can be increased during the year only by a Supplementary Grant voted by Parliament; re-appropriation cannot move funds from one grant to another.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Accounts of the Indian Railways are compiled by the Railway Board from the Account Currents rendered by the zonal railways and other accounting units.
2. The Finance Accounts of the Railways are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts, in the same manner as the accounts of the other Ministries.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Statement 1 is correct: the Railway Board compiles the Finance Accounts of the Railways from the Account Currents rendered by the zonal railways and other accounting units. Statement 2 is false: the Controller General of Accounts does not compile the railway accounts.

q: The Estimates Committee, while examining the estimates of a Ministry, does NOT go into:

options.A: The economies that can be effected in the implementation of the estimates
options.B: The merits of the policy underlying the estimates, the policy itself being a matter for Parliament
options.C: The organisation and efficiency of the Ministry
options.D: The form in which the estimates are presented to Parliament

e: The Estimates Committee examines how the estimates are implemented and what economies are possible, but it does not go into the merits of the policy underlying the estimates, since policy itself is a matter for Parliament.

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament was first constituted in the year:
e: The Committee on Public Undertakings was first constituted in the year 1964.

q: The members of the Public Accounts Committee are chosen by the two Houses of Parliament:

options.A: By nomination by the Speaker and the Chairman respectively
options.B: By election by a simple majority vote in each House
options.C: By nomination by the Finance Minister
options.D: By election in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote

e: The members of the Public Accounts Committee are elected by each House in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

q: Which of the following is NOT eligible to be a member of the Public Accounts Committee?

options.A: A member of the Rajya Sabha
options.B: A member belonging to an Opposition party in the Lok Sabha
options.C: A Minister in the Council of Ministers
options.D: A member who is also a member of the Estimates Committee

e: A Minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee, because the Committee scrutinises the expenditure of the Government of which the Minister forms a part.

q: In relation to the Public Accounts Committee, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is often described as the Committee's:

options.A: Chairman and convenor

e: The Comptroller and Auditor General assists the Public Accounts Committee with his audit reports and expert guidance and is therefore described as the Committee's friend, philosopher and guide.

q: The Departmentally Related Standing Committees of Parliament, which examine the Demands for Grants of the Ministries, were set up in the year:
e: The Departmentally Related Standing Committees, which examine the Demands for Grants of the Ministries, were set up in the year 1993.

q: Rent and licence fees realised from outside parties for the use of railway land and buildings are classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Passenger Earnings

e: Rent and licence fees realised for the use of railway land and buildings are miscellaneous local receipts, classified under Sundry Other Earnings rather than under any traffic earnings head.

q: Since the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the expenditure of the Railways for the initial part of a financial year, pending the voting of the Demands for Grants, is authorised through:

options.A: A separate Vote on Account taken exclusively for the Railways
options.B: The Railway Board's own budget orders
options.C: The common Vote on Account granted for the Government of India as a whole
options.D: Advances from the Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: Since the merger, expenditure for the initial part of the year pending the voting of Demands is authorised through the common Vote on Account granted for the Government of India as a whole; there is no separate railway Vote on Account.

q: An imprest (permanent advance) held by a railway officer is treated in the accounts, until the holder renders an account of the expenditure incurred out of it, as:

options.A: Final expenditure of the railway
options.B: A deposit received from the officer
options.C: A part of the cash balance of the Cash & Pay Office
options.D: An advance outstanding against the holder

e: An imprest is a permanent advance held by an officer; until he renders an account of the expenditure incurred out of it, the amount remains an advance outstanding against the holder and not final expenditure.

q: The original grant under a Demand is Rs 2,400 crore. During the year, a supplementary grant of Rs 150 crore is obtained and funds of Rs 90 crore are surrendered. The Final Grant for the Demand is:

options.A: Rs 2,340 crore

e: Working: Final Grant = 2,400 + 150 - 90 = Rs 2,460 crore.

q: The Final Grant under a Demand for a year is Rs 1,150 crore and the actual expenditure booked against the Demand is Rs 1,212 crore. The excess expenditure requiring regularisation through an Excess Grant is:

options.A: Rs 52 crore

e: Working: Excess expenditure = 1,212 - 1,150 = Rs 62 crore, which requires regularisation through an Excess Grant.

q: Through-traffic earnings of Rs 24,000 are to be apportioned among Railways X, Y and Z in proportion to the distances travelled over them, namely 1,000 km, 600 km and 400 km respectively. The share of Railway Z is:
e: Working: Total distance = 1,000 + 600 + 400 = 2,000 km. Share of Railway Z = 24,000 x 400/2,000 = Rs 4,800.

q: The Final Grant under a Demand is Rs 950 crore and the actual expenditure is Rs 874 crore. The saving, expressed as a percentage of the Final Grant, is:

options.A: 8 per cent

e: Working: Saving = 950 - 874 = Rs 76 crore. Saving as percentage of Final Grant = 76/950 x 100 = 8 per cent.

q: The sanctioned cost of a work is Rs 750 crore. Expenditure of Rs 410 crore has been incurred on it up to the end of the previous year and an outlay of Rs 140 crore is provided in the current year. The throw-forward of the work at the end of the current year will be:

options.A: Rs 340 crore

e: Working: Throw-forward = Sanctioned cost - Expenditure already incurred - Current year's outlay = 750 - 410 - 140 = Rs 200 crore.

q: The annual allotment for a head of account is Rs 1,240 crore and the budget proportion fixed for the first quarter of the year is 30 per cent. The proportionate allotment for the first quarter is:

options.A: Rs 310 crore

e: Working: Proportionate allotment = 30 per cent of Rs 1,240 crore = Rs 372 crore.

q: The annual plan outlay of the Railways is Rs 3,60,000 crore. It is financed by Gross Budgetary Support of Rs 2,10,000 crore and Extra Budgetary Resources of Rs 90,000 crore. The balance met from the internal resources of the Railways is:

options.A: Rs 50,000 crore

e: Working: Internal resources = 3,60,000 - 2,10,000 - 90,000 = Rs 60,000 crore.

q: The annual allotment for a head of account is Rs 2,000 crore. The budget proportions fixed for the first and second quarters are 20 per cent and 25 per cent respectively. The total proportionate allotment available up to the end of the second quarter is:

options.A: Rs 900 crore

e: Working: Combined proportion for the two quarters = 20 per cent + 25 per cent = 45 per cent. Proportionate allotment up to the second quarter = 45 per cent of Rs 2,000 crore = Rs 900 crore.

q: The original grant under a Demand is Rs 900 crore. During the year, a supplementary grant of Rs 120 crore is obtained, and funds of Rs 30 crore are also re-appropriated to the Demand from another head within the same grant. The Final Grant for the Demand is:

options.A: Rs 1,050 crore

e: Working: Final Grant = 900 + 120 = Rs 1,020 crore. The re-appropriation of Rs 30 crore is only a transfer between heads within the same grant, so it does not change the total grant.

q: The original grant under a Demand is Rs 1,000 crore and a supplementary grant of Rs 100 crore is obtained during the year. The actual expenditure booked against the Demand is Rs 1,060 crore. The position at the close of the year is:

options.A: An excess of Rs 60 crore, requiring regularisation through an Excess Grant
options.B: A saving of Rs 40 crore, there being no excess over the Final Grant
options.C: An excess of Rs 100 crore, requiring regularisation through an Excess Grant
options.D: A saving of Rs 60 crore, there being no excess over the Final Grant

e: Working: Final Grant = 1,000 + 100 = Rs 1,100 crore. Actual expenditure of Rs 1,060 crore is within the Final Grant, leaving a saving of Rs 40 crore and no excess to regularise.

q: Under Article 117(3) of the Constitution, a Bill which, if enacted and brought into operation, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India shall not be passed by either House of Parliament unless:

options.A: The President has recommended to that House the consideration of the Bill
options.B: The Speaker has certified that the Bill is a Financial Bill
options.C: The Finance Minister has concurred in the provisions of the Bill
options.D: The Bill has first been examined by the Estimates Committee

e: Under Article 117(3), a Bill which would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India cannot be passed by either House unless the President has recommended the consideration of the Bill to that House.

q: The recommendations made by the Finance Commission under Article 280 of the Constitution are laid before each House of Parliament:

options.A: By the Finance Minister, along with the Demands for Grants
options.B: By the President, together with an explanatory memorandum as to the action taken thereon
options.C: By the Chairman of the Finance Commission in person
options.D: By the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are caused to be laid before each House of Parliament by the President, together with an explanatory memorandum as to the action taken on them.

q: Under Article 282 of the Constitution, the Union or a State may make grants:

options.A: Only for purposes falling within its own legislative competence
options.B: Only for the purposes enumerated in the Union List or the State List, as the case may be
options.C: For any public purpose, even if that purpose is not one with respect to which it may make laws
options.D: Only with the prior approval of the Finance Commission

e: Article 282 empowers the Union or a State to make grants for any public purpose, even if that purpose is not one with respect to which it may make laws.

q: The Macro-Economic Framework Statement, laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act along with the Budget, primarily sets out:

options.A: The head-wise estimates of expenditure of every Ministry
options.B: The provisions of the Finance Bill explained clause by clause
options.C: The certified accounts of the previous year
options.D: An assessment of the growth prospects of the economy, along with the specific underlying assumptions

e: The Macro-Economic Framework Statement under the FRBM Act sets out an assessment of the growth prospects of the economy along with the specific underlying assumptions.

q: The members of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament hold office for a term of:

options.A: One year
options.D: The remaining term of the Lok Sabha

e: The members of the Public Accounts Committee hold office for a term of one year.

q: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is:

options.A: Elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves
options.B: Appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the Lok Sabha members of the Committee
options.D: The senior-most member of the Committee, by convention

e: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the Lok Sabha members of the Committee.

q: The Public Accounts Committee of Parliament was first set up in the year:
e: The Public Accounts Committee was first set up in the year 1921.

q: The Estimates Committee of Parliament was first constituted in the year:
e: The Estimates Committee was first constituted in the year 1950.

q: The reports of the Estimates Committee are presented to:

options.A: The Lok Sabha only

e: The reports of the Estimates Committee are presented to the Lok Sabha only, as the Committee is a committee of that House.

q: The administrative expenses of the Election Commission of India are:

options.A: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Voted by Parliament, as part of the Demands for Grants of the Government
options.C: Met out of the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Charged on the Public Account of India

e: The administrative expenses of the Election Commission are voted by Parliament as part of the Demands for Grants; they are not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: When a Money Bill, after being passed by the Lok Sabha, is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, there is endorsed on it:

options.A: The assent of the President of India
options.B: The recommendations of the Finance Commission
options.C: The certificate of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, signed by him, that it is a Money Bill
options.D: The certificate of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: When a Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, it bears the certificate of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, signed by him, that it is a Money Bill.

q: The estimates of the receipts of the Government, as presented in the Annual Financial Statement, are:

options.A: Voted by the Lok Sabha along with the Demands for Grants
options.C: Approved by the President without reference to Parliament
options.D: Not subjected to a vote of Parliament; it is only the Demands for Grants for expenditure that are voted by the Lok Sabha

e: The estimates of receipts in the Annual Financial Statement are not subjected to a vote of Parliament; only the Demands for Grants for expenditure are voted, and that too by the Lok Sabha alone.

q: The audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India to verify that the moneys shown in the accounts as having been disbursed were legally available for, and were applied to, the services and purposes for which the grants and appropriations were made by Parliament is known as:

options.A: Appropriation audit

e: Appropriation audit verifies that the moneys shown in the accounts as disbursed were legally available for, and were applied to, the services and purposes for which the grants and appropriations were made.

q: In the terminology of the Railways' Works Programme, 'LAW' stands for:

options.A: List of Anticipated Works

e: In the terminology of the Railways' Works Programme, 'LAW' stands for List of Approved Works.

q: Expenditure incurred on a work or service without obtaining the sanction of the authority competent to sanction that expenditure is termed:

options.A: Unauthorised expenditure

e: Expenditure incurred without obtaining the sanction of the competent authority is termed unsanctioned expenditure; it is distinct from excess expenditure, which is expenditure over a sanctioned grant.

q: The Debt Head Report rendered by a zonal railway, showing the balances under the debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads, is prepared from:

options.A: The station balance sheets rendered by the stations
options.B: The bank scrolls received from the accredited bank
options.C: The Works Registers maintained in the Accounts Office
options.D: The balances as recorded in the General Ledger (General Books) of the railway

e: The Debt Head Report is prepared from the balances as recorded in the General Ledger (General Books) of the railway, which record the balances under the debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads.

q: The March (Final) Account Current rendered by a zonal railway, following the March (Preliminary) Account Current, serves mainly to:

options.A: Incorporate the adjustments and corrections received after the rendering of the March (Preliminary) account, so that the accounts of the financial year are closed completely and correctly
options.B: Present the Budget Estimates of the following year to the Railway Board
options.C: Report the approximate earnings of the month of March
options.D: Obtain the supplementary grant for the month of March

e: The March (Final) Account Current incorporates the adjustments and corrections received after the March (Preliminary) Account Current is rendered, so that the accounts of the financial year are closed completely and correctly.

q: Stores issued from a stores depot to a revenue work are credited in the accounts to:

options.A: Manufacturing Suspense

e: Stores issued from a stores depot are credited to Stores Suspense, the head which is debited when stores are received into stock, so that its balance reflects the value of stores in stock.

q: The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, under which the declared provisions of the Finance Bill relating to certain duties take effect immediately on the introduction of the Bill, was enacted in the year:
e: The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, under which the declared provisions of the Finance Bill relating to certain duties take effect immediately on the introduction of the Bill, was enacted in the year 1931.

q: Which of the following grants, made by Parliament under Article 116 of the Constitution, is often described as a 'blank cheque' given to the Government, because, on account of the magnitude or the indefinite character of the service, the demand cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Demand for Grant?

options.A: Vote on Account

e: A Vote of Credit, granted under Article 116, is described as a 'blank cheque' because, owing to the magnitude or indefinite character of the service, the demand cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Demand for Grant.

q: For capital (works) expenditure of the Railways, the unit of appropriation is:

options.A: The Plan Head

e: For capital (works) expenditure of the Railways, the unit of appropriation is the Plan Head, against which grants are voted and expenditure is controlled.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Capital' from the 'Capital Fund' in railway finance?

options.A: 'Capital' denotes the amounts of the Capital Fund invested in works, whereas the 'Capital Fund' denotes budgetary support from the General Finances
options.B: 'Capital' denotes the capital provided to the Railways by the General Finances (Gross Budgetary Support), whereas the 'Capital Fund' is a fund created out of the Railways' own internal resources, principally the surplus, for financing capital works
options.C: There is no difference between the two; the terms are interchangeable
options.D: 'Capital' is a source of revenue receipts, whereas the 'Capital Fund' is a part of the Consolidated Fund of India

e: 'Capital' denotes the capital provided to the Railways by the General Finances as Gross Budgetary Support, whereas the Capital Fund is a fund created out of the Railways' own internal resources, principally the surplus, for financing capital works.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the monthly 'Account Current' of a zonal railway from the 'Trial Balance'?

options.A: The Account Current is an internal statement of ledger balances, whereas the Trial Balance is the account rendered to the Railway Board
options.B: The Account Current is prepared only at the close of the year, whereas the Trial Balance is prepared every month
options.C: The Account Current is the monthly account of the receipts and disbursements of the railway rendered to the Railway Board, whereas the Trial Balance is a statement of the balances of the Ledger accounts, prepared within the Accounts Office to prove the arithmetical accuracy of the books
options.D: The Account Current relates only to the suspense heads, whereas the Trial Balance relates only to the earnings of the railway

e: The Account Current is the monthly account of receipts and disbursements rendered by a zonal railway to the Railway Board, whereas the Trial Balance is an internal statement of Ledger balances prepared to prove the arithmetical accuracy of the books.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'approximate earnings' from 'accounted earnings' of the Railways?

options.A: Approximate earnings relate to goods traffic only, whereas accounted earnings relate to coaching traffic only
options.B: Approximate earnings are compiled by the Railway Board, whereas accounted earnings are compiled by the stations
options.C: Approximate earnings are the final audited figures, whereas accounted earnings are provisional figures
options.D: Approximate earnings are the provisional figures compiled at short intervals from the station returns, before internal check and apportionment, whereas accounted earnings are the final figures brought to account after check and apportionment, as compiled in the Traffic Book

e: Approximate earnings are the provisional figures compiled at short intervals from station returns, before internal check and apportionment, whereas accounted earnings are the final figures brought to account after check and apportionment, as compiled in the Traffic Book.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, Major Heads 8658 (Suspense Accounts) and 8675 (Deposits with Reserve Bank) fall under the 'Suspense and Miscellaneous' section of the Public Account of India.
2. Major Head 8782 (Cash Remittances and adjustments between officers rendering accounts to the same accounting authority) falls under the 'Remittances' section of the Public Account of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Both statements are correct: Major Heads 8658 (Suspense Accounts) and 8675 (Deposits with Reserve Bank) fall under the 'Suspense and Miscellaneous' section of the Public Account, and Major Head 8782 falls under the 'Remittances' section.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Supplementary estimates for expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India are presented to the Lok Sabha along with the Supplementary Demands for Grants.
2. Like all charged expenditure, such charged supplementary estimates are not submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Both statements are correct: supplementary estimates for charged expenditure are presented to the Lok Sabha along with the Supplementary Demands for Grants, but like all charged expenditure they are not submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Commission is constituted by the President at the expiration of every fifth year, or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary.
2. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are binding on the Government of India and must be implemented without any modification.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Statement 1 is correct: the Finance Commission is constituted by the President at the expiration of every fifth year, or earlier if the President considers it necessary. Statement 2 is false: the Commission's recommendations are advisory and not binding on the Government.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Estimates Committee takes up for examination the estimates of only such Ministries, departments or subjects as it selects each year, and not the estimates of all the Ministries in a single year.
2. The Estimates Committee itself votes the Demands for Grants after examining them, whereafter the Lok Sabha passes them without further discussion.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Statement 1 is correct: the Estimates Committee selects only certain Ministries, departments or subjects for examination each year and does not cover all Ministries in one year. Statement 2 is false: the Committee does not vote the Demands; they are voted by the Lok Sabha.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Balance Sheet of the Railways, the balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads are netted head-wise and only the net balance under each head is shown.
2. Credit balances under such heads, representing amounts payable by the Railways, are shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Statement 1 is false: in the Railway Balance Sheet the debit and credit balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads are shown separately and are not netted head-wise. Statement 2 is correct: credit balances represent amounts payable by the Railways and appear on the liabilities side.

q: The subsidiary books of a railway, in which the transactions are first recorded in detail before being compiled into the General Books, are also known as the books of:

options.A: Final entry

e: The subsidiary books in which transactions are first recorded in detail, before compilation into the General Books, are the books of original entry, also called books of prime entry.
